fact: The education ministry inaugurated a modernised State Exam grading centre in Kinshasa on 10 April 2025 running the AI-using software Snote Manager to process test items.

PATH, with the Ministry of Health, piloted SnapiForm, an AI tool reading paper health registers into DHIS2, in 12 DRC health zones for several months; PATH reports reporting time fell from over two hours to about 15 minutes.
Education minister Raissa Malu told the Council of Ministers on 15 August 2025 that an AI system automated exam-paper marking in 2025, with results published three days after the exams.
Minister Malu reported AI exam processing cut processing time by 30-40 percent, raised speed tenfold, and lifted scanning from 8-10 to 80-100 papers a minute.
